## Title

`Program: Attendee can see the correct organizer-configured label on the Side Drawer tab in the Session Calendar so that the terminology is consistent with the rest of the event`

---

## Background / Context

> **This is a fix to an existing feature.** The Session Calendar Side Drawer currently hardcodes the tab label **"By Track"**. ExpoPlatform allows event organizers to rename the Tracks filter via **Admin Panel → Sessions → Display Filters** (e.g. renaming "Tracks" to "Streams", "Topics", "Themes"). This configured label is already respected elsewhere in the platform but is not being picked up in the Session Calendar Side Drawer tab, causing a label inconsistency for clients who have customised this value.

![](blob:https://media.staging.atl-paas.net/?type=file&localId=06d7b81cf1c9&id=03aad9b2-a298-4f03-b75b-283aaabfa4dc&&collection=&height=1099&occurrenceKey=null&width=1610&__contextId=null&__displayType=null&__external=false&__fileMimeType=null&__fileName=null&__fileSize=null&__mediaTraceId=null&url=null)
---

## User Story

As an **Attendee**,  
I want to **see the correct filter label on the Side Drawer tab in the Session Calendar** (during **Live event / Pre-event**),  
so that **the terminology shown to me is consistent with how the organizer has named their filters across the rest of the event**.

---

## Acceptance Criteria (testable + glossary nouns only)

### 1. Side Drawer Tab Label Reflects Organizer-Configured Display Filter Name

* **Given** I am an **Attendee** viewing the Session Calendar and the organizer has **not** customised the Tracks filter label in **Admin Panel → Sessions → Display Filters**, **when** I open the Side Drawer, **then** the tab displays the default label **"By Track"**.
* **Given** the organizer has renamed the Tracks filter to a custom label (e.g. **"Streams"**), **when** I open the Side Drawer in the Session Calendar, **then** the tab displays **"By Streams"** instead of "By Track".

### 2. Localized Custom Label is Respected

* **Given** the organizer has provided a localized version of the custom Display Filter label, **when** an **Attendee** views the Session Calendar in that language, **then** the Side Drawer tab displays the localized version of the custom label.

---

## Out of Scope

Not included:

* Renaming any other labels or tabs beyond the "By Track" Side Drawer tab in the Session Calendar
* Changes to the Side Drawer layout or content
* Admin Panel UI changes to the Display Filter settings

cc <custom data-type="mention" data-id="id-1">@Elena Potapov</custom>   
Alphabetical Order for Tracks, Tags and Types Options

### Background

German organizers are concerned that it is difficult for users to browse options in Tracks, Types and Tags. They want these options to be sorted alphabetically. For multilingual events, each language must have its own alphabetical order.

### What needs to be done

#### Add new setting

In **Admin Panel → Management → Sessions → Config → General settings**, add a new toggle:

* **"Alphabetical order for Tracks, Tags and Types options"**
* Default value: **OFF**

#### Behavior when enabled — Admin Panel

* In **Admin Panel → Management → Sessions**, options in the **Tracks**, **Tags** and **Types** sections are sorted alphabetically automatically.
* Sorting is applied **per edit language** — each language has its own alphabetical order based on its translated values.
* When a new option is added, it is automatically placed into its alphabetical position after save.
* Manual reordering of options is **disabled** in the Tracks, Tags and Types sections.
* A helptext is displayed in these sections:

    _"Automatic alphabetical order for options is enabled, if you want to reorder options manually switch off automatic alphabetical order for options in Config section"_



#### Behavior when disabled after being enabled

* Automatic sorting stops being applied.
* Options **remain in the last sorted order — alphabetical based on the English version** — they do not revert to their pre-sorting order.
* Manual reordering becomes available again.

#### Behavior when enabled — Frontend

The sorted order for the chosen language is reflected in:

* **Sessions lists**: All Sessions, Round Tables, On-Demand — Tracks, Tags and Types options are ordered alphabetically.
* **Marketplace → Exhibitor Events list** — Tracks, Tags and Types options are ordered alphabetically.
* The same applies to these lists in the **mobile app**.

### ✅ Acceptance Criteria

#### Admin Panel — Setting

**Given** an Organizer opens Admin Panel → Management → Sessions → Config  
**When** they view the General settings section  
**Then** the "Alphabetical order for Tracks, Tags and Types options" toggle is displayed and is OFF by default.

#### Admin Panel — Sorting

**Given** the setting is ON  
**When** the Organizer opens the Tracks, Tags or Types section in Admin Panel → Management → Sessions  
**Then** the options are sorted alphabetically for the currently selected edit language.

**Given** the setting is ON and the event is multilingual  
**When** the Organizer switches the edit language  
**Then** the options are re-sorted alphabetically according to the translated values of that language.

**Given** the setting is ON  
**When** the Organizer adds a new Track, Tag or Type option and saves  
**Then** the new option is automatically placed into its alphabetical position.

#### Admin Panel — Manual reordering lock

**Given** the setting is ON  
**When** the Organizer opens the Tracks, Tags or Types section  
**Then** the ability to change the order of options manually is disabled.

**Given** the setting is ON  
**When** the Organizer views the Tracks, Tags or Types section  
**Then** the following helptext is displayed: _"Automatic alphabetical order for options is enabled, if you want to reorder options manually switch off automatic alphabetical order for options in Config section"_.

**Given** the setting is turned OFF after being ON  
**When** the Organizer opens the Tracks, Tags or Types section  
**Then** manual reordering is available again and the helptext is not displayed.

#### Admin Panel — Toggle OFF behavior

**Given** the setting is turned OFF after being ON  
**When** the Organizer views the Tracks, Tags or Types sections  
**Then** options remain in the last sorted order (alphabetical based on the English version) across all languages, and no automatic sorting is applied to subsequent changes.

**Given** the setting is OFF and a new option is added  
**When** the Organizer saves it  
**Then** the option is not sorted automatically and is placed according to current (non-sorted) ordering behavior.

#### Frontend — Web

**Given** the setting is ON and a user has language X selected  
**When** they open All Sessions, Round Tables or On-Demand lists  
**Then** Tracks, Tags and Types options are displayed in alphabetical order for language X.

**Given** the setting is ON and a user has language X selected  
**When** they open the Marketplace → Exhibitor Events list  
**Then** Tracks, Tags and Types options are displayed in alphabetical order for language X.

#### Frontend — Mobile App

**Given** the setting is ON  
**When** a user opens the Sessions lists or Exhibitor Events list in the app  
**Then** Tracks, Tags and Types options are ordered alphabetically for the chosen language, consistent with web.

comments.author: Kavinder Rawal
comments.body:
<custom data-type="mention" data-id="id-0">@Olena Khromei</custom>   
Thank you for laying these out so clearly! Here are the answers to resolve the 3 estimation blockers and the 4 test-case criteria:

1. **Platform Scope**:

    * **Scope**: The primary scope of this story is **Admin Panel / Web + Backend API**.
    * **Mobile**: Because the backend API will return the sorted list dynamically, mobile apps consuming the API will inherit the sorted order automatically.   
      <custom data-type="mention" data-id="id-1">@Taimoor Zulfiqar</custom> can you please confirm that no separate story or work is needed from the mobile team?  
    
2. **How the Order is Produced (On-the-Fly vs. Stored)**:

    * **Decision**: **Sorted on-the-fly based on the active locale.**
    * **Reasoning**: Because each language has a different alphabetical order (e.g., German vs. English vs. French), a single static order cannot be pre-saved in DB for all languages. The backend API dynamically sorts the data per request based on the user’s selected interface/edit language.  
    
3. **Manual Order When Toggle is Switched** `OFF`:

    * **Decision**: **Manual order is PRESERVED in DB and RESTORED when toggle is** `OFF`.
    * **Reasoning**: The manual drag-and-drop order in the database stays untouched. The toggle acts as a display override. Turning the toggle `OFF` immediately restores the organiser's original manual drag-and-drop arrangement.  
    

4. **Tracks Displayed Above the List**:

    * **YES**. Alphabetical sorting applies to Tracks everywhere they function as filters—both inside the filter panel dropdowns and as quick-filter chips/tabs above the list.  
    
5. **Character Precedence vs. Locale Rules**:

    * **Locale Collation (ICU Standard) takes precedence.** The system relies on standard ICU (`Intl.Collator`) locale rules per active language, which naturally handle digits, punctuation, and letters for that specific language.  
    
6. **Ties & Deterministic Sorting**:

    * If two items produce identical translated names in the active language (or differ only by casing like _"apple"_ vs _"Apple"_):
    
        1. Standard ICU variant comparison distinguishes case/accents.
        2. **Tie-breaker**: If names are identical, sort by **Entity ID (ascending)** to guarantee deterministic, stable ordering across page reloads.  
        
    
7. **Permissions**:

    * Standard **Sessions Config Permissions**. Any admin role with access to manage `Admin Panel → Management → Sessions → Config` can view and edit the toggle. No new standalone permission node is required.
    

Based on these answers I will update the **Jira ticket description** to reflect all of the above so it serves as the single source of truth for estimation. Let me know if anything needs further clarification!

A clarification about one side effect of the decision to sort on the fly and store nothing in the database — we would like to record it explicitly so it does not come up as a bug during testing.

Besides the filter lists on the website and in the app, the platform has a public API (`/api/v3/events/{eventId}/sessions/tracks`, `/types`, `/tags`) that external systems use to export the tracks, tags and types reference lists. It works differently from the filters on the frontend:

What we do know is that both the order of the records and the `orderNum` field in this API reflect the manual order stored in the database. Since, per the decision taken, the alphabetical order is never stored and is calculated on the fly at display time, this channel will keep returning the manual order regardless of the state of the setting.

The filter payload from `POST /api/v1/search/filters` carries an `order_num` on every `category` item, and the web frontend currently re-sorts the Tracks chips shown above the list by that field — it does not render them in response order. So with the setting ON the filter panel dropdowns would be alphabetical while the chips above the list stay in the manual drag-and-drop order.

<custom data-type="mention" data-id="id-0">@Kavinder Rawal</custom> — adding to Olena's questions. The points below haven't been discussed anywhere yet; I've flagged where the answer affects the estimate.

**1. "Confirmed / cancelled in the last 5 days" counters — how accurate do they need to be?** (+3 days for the accurate option)  
The system doesn't store the date on which a meeting changed status — only its current status and the date it was last modified. That leaves two options. Approximate: a meeting counts towards the figure if it was last modified within those five days, but then any edit — a time change, a location change — is also counted as "confirmed this week". Accurate: we start keeping a status change log, so the numbers are correct, but that adds +3 days of development, and the data only accumulates from release onwards — for the first five days after go-live the counters would be incomplete.

**2. Sending frequency and time — fixed or configurable?** (+2 days for configurable)  
The spec hard-codes 09:00 event time, and the organiser can change neither the time nor the frequency. The client request in EP-47533 asked for exactly that: a choice of frequency (daily / weekly) and of time.

**3. Pending — whose response are we waiting for?**  
The counter covers meeting requests awaiting a reaction. Please confirm which ones: only those awaiting the attendee's own response; only those where the attendee is waiting on someone else; or both together.

**4. An "unsubscribe" link in the email itself.** (+0.5 day)  
The profile toggle exists, but to use it an attendee has to log into the platform and find the setting. For a daily send, an unsubscribe link directly in the email is normally expected. Do we add one?

**5. Module disabled but data exists.**  
The rule "if all blocks are empty, no email is sent" is already covered in the spec. What remains is a narrow case: the attendee's role has messages or meetings disabled, yet data for them formally exists. Do we hide the block — as Campaign emails do — or show it?

comments.author: Maryna Dovgal
comments.body:
<custom data-type="mention" data-id="id-0">@Kavinder Rawal</custom> — a separate proposal on how to implement this. We would like to propose implementing the digest not as a separate template in the Meetings section, but as a new type of campaign.

**Why**

The mechanism becomes universal: the same setup also covers a digest for exhibitors (the client request in EP-47533) and any future recurring digests — an unread messages digest, for example. Nothing has to be developed separately for each audience.

It also answers the reporting question straight away: Campaigns already have a statistics page for every send — how many emails went out, how many were opened, and the list of recipients with search and export. If each daily send is recorded as a separate send event, per-day statistics come for free.

**What already exists in Campaigns and needs no development**

* Audience: visitors by category, exhibitors by category, team members (regular and admin), speakers, moderators. Plus profile-data filters, Meeting Program and Round Tables filters, session filters, and selections such as "activated", "invited", "only with incoming meeting requests".
* An email editor and a separate preview page: you can see how the email looks for a specific attendee, subject line included.
* Language versions of the template, including the subject line per language — the version is picked by the recipient's language.
* Number of items per block: the template editor lets the organiser set how many meetings and chats to show, up to 10 — so "up to 8 meetings" and "up to 10 chats" from the spec both fit.
* Ready-made variables: meetings block, chats block, the attendee's number of meetings, their number of chats, first name, last name, email, company, event name, login link, profile link.
* Send statistics: how many were sent, how many were opened, the recipient list with date and status, search and export.

**What we would build**

1. A recurring schedule — daily or weekly at a given hour.
2. The rule "do not send the email if all blocks are empty".
3. The attendee's personal toggle in profile settings.
4. The Booking Activity block and the 5-day counters.
5. The meetings selection: the existing variable shows incoming requests, whereas the digest needs confirmed meetings for the next 24 hours.
6. Automatic switching of content by event phase: before the event starts the email shows the Booking Activity block, and once the event begins it stops being shown even if the variable is still in the template. Campaigns have no such logic today — the email is assembled from whatever sits in the template, with no link to the event dates.

**So that the digest behaves like a built-in feature rather than an ordinary campaign**

* The "Email Digest" template ships with the platform update and is made non-deletable.
* Creating a second active digest send for the same event is not allowed.
* Duplicate protection: an attendee receives no more than one digest per day, even if something is set up twice.

**What to keep in mind**

* The organiser assembles the send themselves — choosing the audience and the schedule — rather than simply switching a toggle on. This differs from the current spec, where the template lives in the Meetings section and is enabled with a single switch.
* The changes touch a shared module used by all current sends, so a regression check of existing campaigns will be needed.
* Carrying over to new events: the "Email Digest" template will be present on every event — it ships with the platform update and is copied when an event is cloned. The configured send (audience and schedule), however, is not carried over on cloning, so on a new event the digest is off by default: no emails go out until the organiser sets the send up. This matches the spec requirement that the template is off by default.

Would you be open to this approach? If yes, we will come back with the updated estimate for this route.

<custom data-type="mention" data-id="id-0">@Maryna Dovgal</custom>   
This is a great proposal, and moving this into the Campaigns module makes a lot of architectural sense. It cleanly solves several challenges in one go:

* **Reporting & Delivery Logs**: Gives organizers and support full visibility into delivery, opens, and logs without extra UI work.
* **Audience Scope**: Natively supports Attendees and unlocks Exhibitors (<custom data-type="smartlink" data-id="id-1">https://expoplatform.atlassian.net/browse/EP-47533</custom>) and other roles without needing separate builds later.
* **Localization**: Provides multi-language support, custom subject lines, and preview out of the box.

A few questions, guardrails, and design considerations I'd like to align on:

1. **Utilising Existing Designs**: @Nazar Melnyk has already completed the email digest design layouts (dynamic blocks, styling, and card components under <custom data-type="smartlink" data-id="id-2">https://expoplatform.atlassian.net/browse/EP-52511</custom>). We should ensure these exact designs and layouts are fully utilised as the pre-built template structure inside the Campaigns framework.
2. **Unsubscribe Handling**: How will the unsubscribe flow behave under this Campaign approach? Will the standard Campaign email footer token directly toggle off the new "Email Digest" setting in the attendee's profile, or does clicking unsubscribe opt them out of all campaigns/emails? Could you clarify how you envision the one-click unsubscribe vs. preference page working here?
3. **Low-Friction Setup**: Let's make sure we ship a pre-configured, ready-to-use default Digest campaign using Nazar's template so organizers only need to select their audience/time and activate it.
4. **Automated Dynamic Content**: The campaign renderer should handle the phase logic automatically (Booking Activity pre-event vs. Upcoming Meetings during-event) and skip sending if all blocks are empty.
5. **Dispatch Safeguards**: Ensure a hard limit of max 1 digest per participant per day, respecting opt-outs.

Please put together the updated effort estimate and timeline for this approach so we can finalize and lock in the plan.

**For** <custom data-type="mention" data-id="id-0">@Kavinder Rawal</custom> **— your five points**

**1. Utilising Existing Designs.**  
Confirmed: the digest template and all of its blocks are built new, exactly to the EP-52511 layouts.

**2. Unsubscribe Handling.**  
One correction to the starting assumption: there is no standard unsubscribe link in Campaigns today. What exists is the organiser-side exclusion of an account from a send, and the platform-wide address blacklist, which fills automatically from bounces and complaints.

Our proposal: the link in the digest email switches off only the Email Digest setting in the attendee's profile and does not affect the organiser's other emails. We would not build a separate subscription preferences page in the first version — there would be nothing to choose from: ordinary campaigns are one-off sends, and only the digest template can make a send recurring. If such a page is needed later, it sits on top without rework.

**3. Low-Friction Setup.**  
Every event automatically gets a system "Email Digest" send in the "Not active" state: the template is already selected and cannot be changed, the audience is all active visitors, the frequency is daily, the time is 09:00 event time, the end date is the event end date, and the start date is empty. The organiser adjusts audience and time if needed, sets the start date and presses Activate. This send cannot be deleted, and a second one cannot be created.

**4. Automated Dynamic Content.**  
Both parts confirmed. The phase logic sits in the email builder: Booking Activity is rendered only before the event starts. The "all blocks empty — do not send" check sits immediately before dispatch.

**5. Dispatch Safeguards.**  
Confirmed: no more than one digest per attendee per day, enforced by the send log. While the Email Digest toggle in the profile is off, no emails go to that attendee; switch it back on and they receive the next send. The platform-wide blacklist continues to apply on top.

---

**For** <custom data-type="mention" data-id="id-1">@Olena Khromei</custom> **— your points**

**1. When does the digest stop?**  
Covered by the schedule in point 3 above: the send has an end date, defaulting to the event end date, and the organiser can set it earlier. On reaching that date the send moves to "Not active" by itself and emails stop. There are only two states — "Active" and "Not active".

**2. Pending counter — statuses and window.**  
The platform has four statuses: pending, incoming, confirmed, canceled. The spec's "awaiting response" is incoming — a request waiting for the attendee's own answer. We propose counting both directions: requests awaiting the attendee, and the attendee's own requests awaiting others. <custom data-type="mention" data-id="id-2">@Kavinder Rawal</custom>, please confirm this — or we count incoming only.

On the cut-off: request auto-expiry exists in the platform, but it is switched on per event in the meeting settings, so we cannot rely on it. We propose counting only requests whose meeting time has not yet passed — expired ones drop out on their own and no extra setting is needed.

**3. Group chats.**  
We recommend keeping personal chats only in the first version, as the spec says: exhibitor team chats are noisy and the digest would lose its value. <custom data-type="mention" data-id="id-3">@Kavinder Rawal</custom>, your decision is needed here.

**4. Default audience.**  
The draft send targets all active visitors; the organiser adds exhibitors and team members if needed. There will be no previously unsubscribed attendees at launch — the toggle is new. After that the rule is simple: while an attendee's toggle is off, the digest is not sent to them; switch it on and they start receiving it again. The platform-wide blacklist applies on top.

**5. Pre-configured campaign vs. cloning.**  
There is no contradiction. Standard event cloning does not carry sends over — we create the draft ourselves on every event, cloned ones included. We do not carry settings over from the source event: audience filters reference category and session IDs of that specific event, those IDs change on cloning, and carrying them over would mean remapping every identifier. One mistake there would quietly send emails to the wrong audience. The draft is always created with defaults and in the "Not active" state.

---

**On the admin design**

We have the email layouts, but the admin side — the send screen with the repeat setting, start and end dates and the Activate button — has not been designed yet. If the designers have capacity to propose that screen, it would be very welcome. If not, we will build it along existing admin patterns and the designers can review the finished implementation.

<custom data-type="mention" data-id="id-0">@Kavinder Rawal</custom> -- thanks, point by point below.

**1. Dynamic windows.** Agreed. Meetings block = everything up to the next scheduled send; counters = 5 days or the time since the previous send, whichever is longer. For a daily send nothing changes.

**2. Pending.** Agreed: incoming only (awaiting the attendee's own answer), no window on the request date, excluding requests whose meeting time has already passed.

**3. Period label and counters.** Agreed. The backend will supply the real lookback value instead of fixed text. The period label applies only to Confirmed and Cancelled; Pending is a live count and carries no period label. The TOTAL figure and the progress bar -- we're waiting on the layout from Nazar.

**4. First days after release.** Agreed. We hide the Booking Activity block until the log has accumulated the full window. An empty block is better than wrong numbers in the email.

**5. Unsubscribe.** Agreed. The page shown after unsubscribing will have a one-click "turn it back on" option, in case of a mis-click.

**7. Confirmation before activating.** Agreed. Before activation, a dialog showing: the number of recipients, the frequency and selected days, the send time with timezone, the start and end dates, and the date and time of the first email. Plus a live recipient count right on the screen while the audience is being edited.

**8. Statistics.** We propose an aggregate -- one summary for the whole recurring send: totals (sent / opened) plus a recipient list showing, per recipient, how many emails they received, the date of the last one, and whether they opened it; with search and export. This way the screen doesn't hit the 60+ sends over two months -- it's a single summary, not one row per send. It opens the same way, from the three-dot menu on the send's row. Export is of the aggregate; a per-day export and a per-recipient day-by-day drill-down we'll add post-release if needed.

Is the aggregate fine -- or do you need a breakdown per individual send?

**9. Template.** Yes, the template will sit in the Templates List like a normal one, but as a system template: it can't be deleted and its type can't be changed.

**On the timeline.** Yes, the accepted changes move the 18 days. Points 1, 3, 4, 5, 7 together add roughly 3-4 days -> \~21-22 backend days. The main drivers are points 1 and 7, as you noted.

How far we can trim: the per-day export and the per-recipient drill-down are already out of v1 (post-release, no cost now). The only thing we can defer is the "turn it back on" button on the landing page -- that's -0.5 day, i.e. \~20.5-21. Getting closer to 18 isn't possible without dropping the weekly frequency (point 1), which is what drives most of the shift.

We're waiting on your decision on point 8 and your approval of the timeline shift -- after that we take everything into work.

jira.summary: Exhibitor side repeatable entries and multi-file upload
jira.description:
## User Story

**As an** Exhibitor filling out a Manual Form
**I want to** add as many rows as I need to a table section, and upload more than one file to a single File field
**So that** I can submit complete information (e.g. a full machine list, or multiple stand-design documents) without hitting an arbitrary cap or resorting to email

## Background

Table section row counts are currently fixed by the Organizer at setup, and the File element accepts one file per field. Exhibitors with more entries than the configured cap (e.g. 25+ machines vs. a 10-row limit) or documents that need multiple files (e.g. chemical safety sheets plus stand designs) work around this today by emailing the Organizer directly — defeating the point of structured data collection and creating manual work. Raised via FESPA Middle East (Apr 2027, Dubai, \~500 exhibitors) — REQ-2026-075.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] In a table section, the Exhibitor can add a new row on demand, not limited to the Organizer's configured starting row count and upload data in that row which gets saved along with the rest of the entries
- [ ] The Exhibitor can remove a row they added, prior to submission
- [ ] When exhibitor clicks on Add Row, a new row will get created at the bottom of the table where exhibitor will be shown text fields where applicable and fields for entering numbers where applicable. After exhibitor clicks on submit, they cannot edit the row
- [ ] Empty rows should not get submitted
- [ ] A File field accepts multiple uploads, each shown as its own entry and individually removable before submission
- [ ] Existing forms/submissions built with a single fixed row count or single-file fields continue to render and save correctly — no migration needed for historical data
- [ ] The Organizer's view of a submitted Manual Form shows all added rows and all uploaded files, not just the first
- [ ] In Admin Panel > Exhibitor Manual > Manual Settings, when Organizer click on edit file upload button, they will see checkbox to enable or disable multi file upload
- [ ] In Admin Panel > Exhibitor Manual > Manual Settings, when Organizer click on edit table button, they will see checkbox to enable or disable option to allow exhibitor to increase row in exhibitor manual front-end

jira.summary: Exclude surcharge/tax from invoice when offline payment method is selected
jira.description:
Original request: EP-55785 (ACI Asia-Pacific & Middle East, RACE 2027, 11–13 May 2027, Kuala Lumpur). Sample invoice: Derar's comment, 21 Sep 2026.

## Actor

**Delegate** registering for the event and paying for tickets and/or sessions (e.g. "Delegate (ACI-Member) Early Bird Rate", "Pre-Conference Workshop").  
Secondary: **Event admin**, who configures the setting.

## Entry point

Delegate registration journey → checkout → payment method selection. The observable result is on the **generated invoice document (PDF)**, not on the checkout page. The checkout page already stopped showing the surcharge on 31 Aug 2026, whatever the payment method.

## Trigger

The delegate selects **Invoice payment** (the "offline payment" in the client's request) as the payment method and completes the order, and the system generates the invoice.

## Observable outcome

```gherkin
Scenario: Surcharge excluded from the invoice when Invoice payment is selected
  Given the event has the Credit Card Surcharge (4.5%) configured
  And the "exclude for Invoice payment" setting is ON
  When a delegate completes checkout with Invoice payment
  Then the generated invoice shows no Credit Card Surcharge rate or amount on the Tickets and Sessions line items
  And the invoice total equals the net amount with no surcharge added

Scenario: Card payment is unchanged
  Given the event has the Credit Card Surcharge configured
  And the "exclude for Invoice payment" setting is ON
  When a delegate completes checkout with card payment
  Then the invoice shows the Credit Card Surcharge rate and amount exactly as it does today

Scenario: Setting OFF keeps current behaviour
  Given the "exclude for Invoice payment" setting is OFF
  When a delegate completes checkout with Invoice payment
  Then the invoice shows the Credit Card Surcharge exactly as it does today

Scenario: Other taxes are not affected
  Given the event has another tax configured in addition to the Credit Card Surcharge
  And the "exclude for Invoice payment" setting is ON
  When a delegate completes checkout with Invoice payment
  Then only the Credit Card Surcharge is excluded
  And the other tax is still applied and shown on the invoice

Scenario: Totals stay consistent across the platform
  Given an order was placed with Invoice payment and the surcharge was excluded
  Then the order total, the transaction record, the Transaction Dashboard and the Payments report all show the same amount as the invoice

Scenario: Invoices already issued are not changed
  Given invoices were generated before the setting was switched ON
  When the admin switches the setting ON
  Then those existing invoices and transactions are not recalculated or regenerated
```

## Config

* **Where:** Event setup → Payments. ACI's surcharge appears to be set up as a custom tax (see EP-38903), so the control most likely sits on the tax/surcharge configuration. Engineering to confirm.
* **Scope:** per event. It is not hardcoded to ACI.
* **Default:** OFF, so every existing event keeps its current behaviour.
* **Decision needed:** is this a per-tax setting ("do not apply to Invoice payment"), so admins choose which tax is excluded, or one event-level switch? A per-tax setting is recommended, because excluding every tax would also remove a real tax such as VAT/SST.

## Out of scope

Editing the tax/surcharge rate or amount, including Taichi's request to set a flat 5% rate (see EP-55785, 6 Aug comment). That goes to a separate ticket. This story only covers the exclusion.

## Open questions

**Blocking refinement**

1. **Is Invoice payment available in the delegate flow?** Mariia's refinement note says Payments by Invoice is exhibitor-only today (Type = "basket"). ACI's sample invoice shows delegate tickets and sessions, so it needs checking how their delegates reach Invoice payment. If the delegate flow doesn't support it today, adding it is extra scope.
2. **Which build path?** EP-56047 (epic EP-55566, Purchasing module) is rewriting VAT rules and invoice generation and warns against a parallel invoice path. We need to decide whether to build this in the legacy invoice now and accept migration debt, or fold it into the Purchasing module. Either way, link EP-55566 / EP-56047.
3. **What happens when the payment method changes?** For example, the delegate switches from Invoice to card after the invoice was generated, or the admin uses Cancel Payment / Confirm Payment on an invoice-paid order. Recommended default: the invoice reflects the payment method at the time it is generated, and a method change regenerates it with the correct surcharge treatment. Confirm in refinement.
4. **How is the exclusion shown?** Should the surcharge columns be hidden, or shown with 0 / 0.00? Derar's comment allows either. It is also open whether the invoice needs an explicit line such as "No surcharge applied for invoice payment", and in which languages.

**Non-blocking (needed for delivery)**

* A target date. Early bird registration opened in September 2026. We also need to know what ACI does in the meantime.
* Written confirmation from ACI, on the ticket, that the surcharge applies to card payments only and that excluding it for invoice payment is their policy.

comments.author: Mariia Ivanova
comments.body:
Returning this <custom data-type="smartlink" data-id="id-0">https://expoplatform.atlassian.net/browse/EP-56742</custom>  from backlog refinement — the team can't estimate or test it as written. The story has no entry point and no observable outcome, so BE/FE/QA each have to guess a different thing.

**What is needed before re-refinement:**

1. **Actor and flow.** AC1 says "delegate selects offline payment", but Payments by Invoice today is exhibitor-only (Type column is always "basket" ). Is this the delegate registration journey, the exhibitor basket, or both? This changes the estimate several times over.
2. **Terminology.** "Offline payment" isn't a platform term. Suppose it means **Invoice payment** (the `Disable invoice payment` setting in Event setup → Payments → General),
3. **Scope of the exclusion.** **Interaction with the existing tax model.** **Сonfig.** 
4. **Scope vs. what the client asked for.** EP-55785 asked to _exclude **or** edit_ the amount, and Derar's 6 Aug comment records Taichi asking for an **editable tax rate** (they need a flat 5%, the system restricts to 5.5/6.5 increments) — with Rachid already treating this ticket as covering it. This story is exclude-only. Please either extend it or add an explicit Out of scope line plus a separate ticket, so we don't ship something the client reads as the wrong thing.
5. **State transitions.** What happens when the payer switches from invoice to card after the invoice is generated, or when an admin uses Cancel Payment / Confirm Payment? Recalculate? Regenerate the invoice? What about already-issued pending invoices?
6. **Dependency decision.** EP-56047 (under the in-progress EP-55566 epic) is rewriting exactly this ground — discounts, VAT rules and invoice generation — and explicitly warns against building a parallel invoice path. EP-55641 is on hold on a related VAT question. We need your call: build in legacy now and accept the migration debt, or fold this into the Purchasing module. Please link EP-55566 / EP-56047 either way.

**Also needed, non-blocking for refinement but blocking for delivery:**

* The client's actual invoice template — Derar flagged on 31 Jul that the attachment never arrived. AC3 ("the invoice clearly mentions that no tax was applied") can't be specified or translated without it, and our invoices are multilingual.
* A target date, and what ACI does in the meantime. Early bird opened in September 2026; the last timeline update on EP-55785 was "I'll get back to you" on 27 Aug.
* Written confirmation from ACI that excluding VAT based on payment method is their tax policy and their responsibility. VAT normally depends on jurisdiction and buyer status, not on how the buyer pays — I'd like that on the ticket, not only in email.

---

**Proposal — a minimum bar for stories entering refinement**

Suppose it should remove most of what we lose sprint time to:

* **Actor** — the specific role, not "user"
* **Entry point** — the screen or admin URL where it starts
* **Trigger** — what the actor does
* **Observable outcome** — what they see, where, and what changes in the data
* **Config** — where the setting lives and what its default is (for anything configurable)
* **Out of scope** — one line, mandatory

Happy to agree this as the Organizer-team Userstory Refinement Definition of Ready and walk through EP-56742 against it together.
